notes: Account overview: boutique research arm of a large wealth manager; building a centralized research/knowledge portal to serve 400+ analysts across equity/fixed income desks.

Primary ask: enterprise-grade search (RAG) with high-quality reranking. Must support ~300M–500M passages, sub-200ms SLO for end-user query (95th), cost target <= $0.02/query for typical lookup+rerank flow.
Preferred: dedicated capacity for predictable latencies and isolated keys. They explicitly asked for customer-managed KMS + audit logs and per-token billing transparency.
Data residency: must keep primary indexes in US regions for NDA'd research; EU-only subset for London desk. Legal flagged cross-border sync — requires retention & residency clauses.

Tech preferences: hybrid retrieval (BM25/ES) + dense embeddings (1536-d) for recall, then a small neural reranker (quantized 4-bit) for top-100. Want recommendation for batch size, KV cache strategy, and quantization profiles.

Scale notes: ingestion team estimates initial index ~300M passages (~15TB raw), growth to 600M in 12–18 months. Peak QPS target 80–120 (global), baseline 15–25 qps. Need autoscale + predictable burst behavior.
Quote from CTO: 'We can't accept black-box residency or key management. Need explicit HSM/KMS path and full audit trail before we sign.'
Procurement path: security review -> SOW -> procurement committee (2–3 weeks after sec signoff) -> PO. They prefer annual committed capacity with optional burst credits.

Cost sensitivity: modeling shows dedicated cluster + intelligent batching must reduce unit cost by ~3x vs current cloud-hosted experiments. Will compare Redwood Optimize suggestions vs internal knobs.

Evaluation plan: 6-week POC with a 10M passage sample ingestion, measure MRR@10, latency P50/P95, and cost per query. Success metric: P95 end-to-end < 200ms and query cost <= $0.02 at 50 qps simulated load.
Internal AE notes: Jordan and Maya ran technical kickoff 2026-01-18 (FF link). SE to deliver config doc and rough cost model by 2026-02-01 — delayed by legal clarifying KMS requirements.
Meeting cadence: weekly sync (AE+SE+CTO) until security signoff; biweekly after POC starts. Ask: connect infra eng to provisioning team early to avoid a 2-week ops lag.
Stubs/refs: drive/poc-specs-v2 includes sample schema and ingestion checklist; ENGOPS-1129 tracks provisioning request for dedicated cluster prototypes.
Tone: terse notes, lots of checkboxes; they like explicit SLAs and measurable rollback/fallback policies (auto-fallback to smaller model variant on degradation).
